description:
Cycle 4b D13 — operator-only one-shot hard-delete of all active `session_ledger__source_cursor` rows for one source. Removes every cursor row whose `source_id` matches the supplied id. Source-scoped (operator passes one `source_id`); intentionally NOT source-kind-scoped because `source_kind` is not unique (chatgpt_export has one source row per uploaded ZIP, per design v4 §D13).

Why this verb exists. When a source's discovery / event-read cursors have advanced past a point the operator wants to re-walk from — chatgpt-export ZIP re-walk being the immediate Cycle 4 case — the importer's poll loop will skip already-processed sessions because the cursor's `high_water` marker excludes them. Deleting the cursor rows resets the importer's view of source progress so the next poll pass walks the source from scratch. Because the source row itself is preserved, the re-walk re-ingests under the SAME `source_id` → same `session_id`, so the now-enforced `(session_id, external_id)` upsert idempotency (GAP-5) dedups the re-walked events at the event level — for events carrying a non-null `external_id`. PRECONDITION (`confirm=true`): because a legacy null-`external_id` row is NOT covered by that unique (NULLs are DISTINCT), a re-walk would DUPLICATE it — so the verb REFUSES (`confirm=true` raises a ValueError) while any null-`external_id` events remain (the same guard `reset_ingest_state` has). Run `backfill_event_external_ids` to 0 nulls first; the `confirm=false` dry-run reports `null_external_id_count` + `precondition_met`.

Hard-delete, not soft. The cursor rows are removed outright (`is_deleted` is not used) per the operator's soft-delete-is-opt-out principle — a cursor reset has no recovery path, and the re-creation path (`write_cursor`) inserts a fresh row when none exists, so no soft-deleted ghost is needed to revive.

Dry-run gate. Default `confirm=false` returns the structured count envelope — `active_cursor_count_before` (rows currently active for source), `deleted_count=0`, `source_id` echo. Operator inspects, then re-runs with `confirm=true`. Idempotent: re-running on a source with no active cursors returns `deleted_count=0` (not an error).

This verb is `is_discoverable=false` — model cannot find it via `process_search` and never proposes it. Operator-only via the operator bridge.
embedding_description: Operator-only ledger recovery: hard-delete every active __source_cursor row for one source. Source-scoped (NOT source-kind-scoped — chatgpt_export has one source per ZIP). Use to force next poll to re-walk a source from scratch when cursors advanced past a point operator wants to reprocess. The source row is preserved → re-walk re-ingests under the same session_id → the (session_id, external_id) upsert idempotency dedups the re-walk (for events with a non-null external_id). GUARD: the verb REFUSES (confirm=true raises) while any legacy null-external_id events remain — run backfill_event_external_ids first, else a re-walk would duplicate them. Default dry-run; confirm=true.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Cursor-reset outcome for one source. `confirmed=false` is a dry-run reporting `active_cursor_count_before` as the size signal. `confirmed=true` reports `deleted_count` (rows hard-deleted; zero on a source with no active cursors).
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: On `confirmed=true`, confirm the next `trigger_poll` cron firing (within 5 min) walks the source from scratch — the discovery_cursor read returns None, so the plugin yields every external session. Re-ingest runs under the same source_id/session_id, so the (session_id, external_id) upsert idempotency dedups the re-walked events that carry a non-null external_id. A confirmed reset is REFUSED while any null-external_id events remain, so run backfill_event_external_ids to 0 nulls first if the source has un-backfilled history.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: One-shot hard DELETE of `__source_cursor` rows whose `source_id` matches the supplied id and `is_deleted = 0`.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: ValueError 'reset_source_cursor refused: ... legacy event(s) still have a null external_id': the precondition is not met — null-external_id events remain, so a re-walk would duplicate them; run backfill_event_external_ids to 0 nulls first. LedgerRepositoryError: the underlying state_service rejected the DELETE or the dry-run COUNT. Possible causes: schema not yet initialized, state_service unavailable, or transient connection failure.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: If refused for null external_ids, run backfill_event_external_ids to convergence (0 nulls), then retry. Confirm `list_sources` returns the active source roster (proves state_service is responsive). The verb is idempotent — re-run with the same arguments after addressing the underlying state_service issue. If the source_id you passed doesn't exist, the verb returns `deleted_count=0` (no error).
